Here is a creative proposal for the interactive scroll-driven exploded gearbox sequence, grounded in cinematography and web-3D camera principles from your sources.

---

### Executive Summary & Design Strategy

The primary goal is to eliminate the current "small distant strip" issue by moving away from permanent full-assembly framing `[1, 2]`. Instead of shrinking the CAD model to fit DOM typography, we use **perspective camera projection** `[1, 3]`, **macro composition** `[2, 4]`, and **dynamic depth-of-field** `[4]` so the mechanical assembly fills 65%–85% of the viewport while DOM captions occupy dedicated screen space.

To resolve the drivetrain cascade pacing, planet gear orbiting is strictly suppressed until its owning planetary carrier physically separates, and later stages (sun gear, clutch, bearings) are granted proportional scroll distance. Camera motion is governed by **CatmullRom spline paths** `[5]` with **LERP smoothing** `[6, 7]` and deterministic progress binding (`animationPhase` from \\(0.0\\) to \\(1.0\\)), ensuring identical, smooth C1 transitions during forward, reverse, or scrubbed scroll seeks `[8-11]`.

---

### Three Distinct Visual Concepts

```
                  ELEVATED SIDE THREE-QUARTER VIEW
                  
                     +-----------------------+
                     |  DOM Caption Overlay  |
                     +-----------------------+
                            \
                             \  Diagonal Depth Axis
                              v
     [ Housing ] ---> [ Planetary Carrier ] ---> [ Clutch ] ---> [ LCD Readout ]
     (Foreground)       (Active Focus)          (Background)     (End Target)
```

#### Concept 1: "Macro Axial Tracking" (Recommended)
* **Visual Thesis**: A high-impact macro perspective that tracks along the drivetrain axis at a fixed \\(35^\circ\\) elevation, framing active components up close while utilizing blurred foreground housing edges for depth `[2, 12, 13]`.
* **Storyboard (4 Beats)**:
  1. **Beat 1 (0–20% Scroll) — Shell Retraction**: Camera holds an elevated \\(35^\circ\\) side 3/4 angle `[14]`. The outer handle and housing slide left along the axis, passing through the near focal plane to create an occlusion cue `[13]`.
  2. **Beat 2 (20–50% Scroll) — Owning Carrier & Planet Reveal**: The primary planetary carrier emerges. Planet gears remain static until the carrier body clears the outer ring gear, after which they begin their synchronous orbit `[15, 16]`.
  3. **Beat 3 (50–80% Scroll) — Sun, Bearings & Friction Clutch Stack**: The camera trucks along a smooth CatmullRom curve `[5, 14]`, shifting focus (rack focus) from the sun gear to the clutch plates as they explode along the diagonal axis `[4, 13]`.
  4. **Beat 4 (80–100% Scroll) — Reassembly & LCD Lock-In**: The exploded parts compress slightly toward their seated positions while the camera arc-pans to frame the angled digital LCD readout `[17, 18]`.
* **Relative Subject Size**: 65%–85% of viewport frame height `[2]`.
* **Lens & Angle Guidance**: \\(85\text{mm}\\) perspective lens equivalent `[1]`, \\(35^\circ\\) elevation, \\(+25^\circ\\) yaw offset.
* **Focus Transitions & DoF**: Dynamic shallow depth-of-field (\\(f/4\\) to \\(f/8\\)) that racks focus to match the active DOM caption target `[4, 13]`.
* **Foreground/Background Parallax**: Foreground housing chamfers blur past the left frame edge, while background planetary teeth provide dimensional depth `[12, 13]`.
* **Native Viewport Allocation**: \\(250\text{vh}\\) total scroll distance.
* **Narrow Viewport Strategy (\\(390 \times 844\\))**: To avoid shrinking the CAD model, increase camera pitch to \\(45^\circ\\) (more top-down diagonal) to align the diagonal explosion with narrow screen proportions `[1, 19]`. CAD fills \\(70\%\\) of screen width, while DOM captions overlay the lower \\(30\%\\) over a subtle gradient scrim `[13]`.
* **LCD Hook & Reassembly**: On reverse scroll, parts lock back into the housing; on forward completion, the camera settles on a close-up hero angle of the illuminated LCD screen.

---

#### Concept 2: "Helical Orbital Cascade"
* **Visual Thesis**: A continuous, single-direction orbital sweep around the expanding JGun CAD assembly, combining arc rotation with axial camera movement `[14, 17]`.
* **Storyboard (4 Beats)**:
  1. **Beat 1 (0–25% Scroll) — Orbital Anchor & Housing Release**: Camera begins at \\(45^\circ\\) side 3/4 and initiates a signed clockwise orbit around the wrench axis as the housing separates `[17, 18]`.
  2. **Beat 2 (25–55% Scroll) — Stage 1 & 2 Carrier Separation**: Camera maintains orbit while moving axially, capturing the planetary carrier extraction and the sun gear engagement `[14, 20]`.
  3. **Beat 3 (55–80% Scroll) — Multi-Planetary & Clutch Sweep**: Camera sweeps past foreground gear teeth, capturing light catches on bevels and clutch plate surfaces `[13, 21]`.
  4. **Beat 4 (80–100% Scroll) — Settling on LCD Readout**: The orbit dampens using LERP interpolation `[6]`, bringing the camera to rest in front of the angled digital LCD display.
* **Relative Subject Size**: 50%–70% frame fill.
* **Lens & Angle Guidance**: \\(50\text{mm}\\) perspective lens `[1]`, \\(30^\circ\\) constant elevation, \\(180^\circ\\) total orbital arc `[17, 20]`.
* **Focus Transitions & DoF**: Deep depth-of-field (\\(f/16\\)) ensuring the entire exploded stack remains sharp throughout the orbit `[4]`.
* **Foreground/Background Parallax**: Strong rotational parallax as gear teeth rotate across the frame relative to the stationary background `[12, 14]`.
* **Native Viewport Allocation**: \\(300\text{vh}\\) total scroll distance.
* **Narrow Viewport Strategy (\\(390 \times 844\\))**: Retain \\(50\text{mm}\\) FOV; allow the exploded axis to extend vertically across the tall screen ratio while floating DOM captions in top and bottom protected zones `[19]`.
* **LCD Hook & Reassembly**: Reversibility returns the camera along the exact inverse helical curve; forward completion settles directly on the LCD panel.

---

#### Concept 3: "Precision Architectural Cutaway"
* **Visual Thesis**: A high-contrast studio presentation emphasizing sectioned CAD geometry, crisp edge highlights, and strict DOM text alignment `[13, 21]`.
* **Storyboard (4 Beats)**:
  1. **Beat 1 (0–20% Scroll) — Sectioned Shell Retraction**: Outer shell retreats to reveal internal gear teeth under sharp rim lighting `[13, 21]`.
  2. **Beat 2 (20–50% Scroll) — Synchronized Carrier & Sun Extraction**: Planets and sun gear separate in exact \\(1:1\\) physical proportion along the central axis `[15, 16]`.
  3. **Beat 3 (50–80% Scroll) — Clutch & Bearing Stack Detail**: Camera pans to isolate the friction clutch and needle bearings `[14, 18]`.
  4. **Beat 4 (80–100% Scroll) — Final Compression & LCD Lock**: Exploded stack compresses into its final state as the camera frames the torque readout screen.
* **Relative Subject Size**: 55%–75% frame fill.
* **Lens & Angle Guidance**: \\(70\text{mm}\\) telephoto perspective, \\(25^\circ\\) elevation, \\(+30^\circ\\) yaw.
* **Focus Transitions & DoF**: Moderate DoF (\\(f/11\\)) with high-contrast edge highlights `[4, 13]`.
* **Foreground/Background Parallax**: Clean linear depth layering with a protected horizon line `[17]`.
* **Native Viewport Allocation**: \\(220\text{vh}\\) total scroll distance.
* **Narrow Viewport Strategy (\\(390 \times 844\\))**: Anchor CAD to the upper 60% of the viewport and allocate the lower 40% for active DOM measured captions `[19]`.
* **LCD Hook & Reassembly**: Parts snap into place on reverse scroll, ending in a static hero pose on the digital readout.

---

### Low-Cost Preview & Approval Method

Before committing to full Three.js implementation or final rendering, produce a **lightweight styleframe animatic** `[22-25]`:
1. **3–4 Static CAD Styleframes**: Render high-resolution viewport stills showing:
   * *Frame A*: Initial hero assembly pose at \\(35^\circ\\) side 3/4 `[14]`.
   * *Frame B*: Peak explosion state highlighting planetary carriers and sun gear `[15]`.
   * *Frame C*: Close-up macro detail showing gear tooth edge lighting and depth-of-field `[4, 13]`.
   * *Frame D*: Final resting shot framed on the angled digital LCD readout.
2. **Short Scroll Clip**: Compile these keyframes into a 5-second WebM/MP4 preview video or interactive Figma scroll prototype to confirm pacing, caption spacing, and camera framing before code integration `[19, 23]`.

---

### Recommendation & Trade-Off Analysis

* **Recommended Concept**: **Concept 1 ("Macro Axial Tracking")**.
* **Why it Wins**: Concept 1 directly solves the core problem: it brings the user close to the mechanical CAD details (filling 65%–85% of the frame) `[2]` while maintaining an elevated \\(35^\circ\\) side 3/4 angle `[14]`. It delivers a memorable portfolio piece without requiring bullet-time effects `[26]`.
* **Main Trade-Off**: Because the CAD model occupies a large portion of the viewport, camera focus (\\(f/4\\)–\\(f/8\\)) and DOM text placement must be tightly coordinated so active captions do not obscure critical moving gear teeth `[4, 13]`.

---

### Distinction: Source-Backed Cinematography vs. Creative Inferences

| Source-Backed Cinematography Principles | Project-Specific Creative Inferences |
| :--- | :--- |
| **Perspective vs. Orthographic Camera**: Perspective projection selected for close-up zooms and interactive 3D depth `[1, 3]`. | **Exact Angle Pick**: \\(35^\circ\\) elevation and \\(+25^\circ\\) yaw vector for the side 3/4 orientation. |
| **Spline-Based Path Math**: Parametric spline curves (`CatmullRomCurve3`) with \\(t \in [27]\\) `[5, 8]`. | **Sequence Pacing**: Allocating specific scroll percentages (e.g., 20%–50% for Stage 1 carrier). |
| **Smooth Curve Transitions**: Look-ahead target offsets (\\(t + 0.06\\)) or dual splines to guarantee C1 continuity `[9, 28]`. | **Part Identity Mapping**: Linking DOM captions specifically to JGun carrier/sun gear components. |
| **Deterministic Scroll Sync**: Linking frame progress (`animationPhase`) to scroll state for seek reversibility `[8, 10, 11]`. | **Scroll Budget**: Setting \\(250\text{vh}\\) as the native scroll allocation. |
| **Smoothing (LERP)**: Linear interpolation to eliminate jitter during rapid mouse/touch scrolling `[6, 7]`. | **Mobile Gradient Scrim**: Using a 30% bottom scrim overlay on narrow viewports. |
| **Macro Depth & Lighting**: Rim/backlighting to catch metallic edges, combined with DoF for visual focus `[2, 4, 13, 21]`. | **LCD Readout End Frame**: Selecting the digital torque readout as the final resting hook. |
| **Pre-production Preview**: Validating styleframes/animatics before full CGI execution `[22-25]`. | |

*(Note: These unrendered concepts represent creative design proposals and have not yet undergone physical web-GL rendering or build verification.)*
